Rules for leash checks
You will learn on this page how the first steps go

This page explains why the first checks matter at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. Early checks protect the animal, reduce delay, and help the trip begin in a controlled way. New staff should treat the leash check as a safety task, not a routine formality, because a secure lead supports calm movement through the terminal and during handoff.

Start by observing the traveler and the animal together. Look for a leash that is fitted correctly, held firmly, and free of visible damage. The animal should remain under steady control, with no pulling, twisting, or loose attachment. If the lead appears weak, tangled, or too short for safe handling, pause the process and ask for a review before continuing. Use clear, respectful language so the traveler understands the concern without feeling rushed.

Keep your attention on the whole picture, not only the equipment. A leash check also helps you notice agitation, fatigue, or other signs that the animal needs a slower pace. If the traveler seems uncertain, give calm guidance and explain each step in simple terms. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey, and your tone should support that standard from the first contact.

When a situation does not fit the normal pattern, move to escalation without delay but without urgency in your voice. The next staff member should receive a concise summary of what you saw, what was checked, and what remains open. <<FACT F051>> Continue with the same steady method after the insertion and keep the focus on safe transfer.

In some cases the pet cabin review will also shape how you proceed at the desk. <<FACT F042>> Use that information only as part of the wider safety picture, and keep your explanation brief and practical for the traveler. Do not overload the conversation with extra detail when a simple instruction is enough.

Remember that careful first steps set the tone for the entire trip, so check, speak, and escalate with steady attention every time.
